artboards.title: The gesture — the handle on a checkbox line
One box on the line, and what the chip keeps
How the picker is reached — B chosen

annotations.text:
WHAT THIS IS AIMING AT

1. The reference in the file becomes [#D-9] instead of a bare D-9.

2. Hovering a checkbox line shows a Sync handle, which opens a searchable picker grouped by project — instead of typing / inside a table cell.

3. A synced line carries ONE box, and it is the deliverable's. Ticking it ticks the Project tab; ticking the Project tab writes the marker back into the file.

SETTLED SO FAR: scope means this fortnight first (widen in one press); the trigger is the hover handle, not a selection popup; the deliverable owns the tick and the file follows.

STILL OPEN: what the chip's label reads, and whether the old bare D-42 keeps being read.

"ALL THE DELIVERABLES IN SCOPE" — CONFIRMED

This fortnight's first, the whole roadmap one press away, counts on both.

In scope = what the panel on the right of the Sprint tab already lists: deliverables in phases overlapping the sprint's dates. 7 of them in a typical fortnight, against 33 in the roadmap.

Grouped by project, sub-labelled by phase, in the same lane colours the scope panel uses.

WHY THE SECOND BOX GOES

Today a synced line draws two: the line's own [ ] and the chip's, which is the deliverable's. Nothing said which one you meant, and the near one — the one at the front of the line, where your thumb is — was the one that meant nothing outside the file.

So the chip hands its tick to the line. A table row is the exception and keeps the chip's box: a row has no box of its own to hand it to.

SETTLED — THE FILES ALREADY ON DISK

sprints/*.md contain bare D-42 today. A was chosen and is what shipped.

A (drawn here). Read both spellings, write only [#D-9]. Nothing on disk is touched. Matches the editor's own precedent — it reads both "- [ ]" and "☐" and writes only the first.

B. Hard switch plus a one-off rewrite of sprints/*.md. One spelling; it edits your gitignored files, so it runs once, against a backup.

C. New spelling only, old stops linking. Least code, silent breakage.

The amber D-11 at the foot of the file is an old reference still being read — that is A.

THE FOUNDATION — NOW BUILT

A reference on a checkbox line already DREW a chip — the renderer is shared with table cells. But sprint_task_refs in main.py walks table blocks only, so that reference never reaches /api/sprints/{n}/links.

Consequence today: no "↗ 03" badge on the Project tab, and the "named in N rows" count misses it.

With the tick moved onto the line, this stops being cosmetic: direction 2 of the write-through needs to know which line of which file to flip, and only the links reader can say.

So main.py reading list lines is the foundation of the whole feature, not a nicety.
